title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 21. Grace to Ramadasa
html:
Jagannatha returns from Gundicha; the Lord sends home the devotees of Gauda and sends Nityananda to Bengal; a poor brahmana from Dravida and Vibhishana at Gaura's feet

Verse 1

एवं दिनत्रयं तत्र भक्तेश्वरविभावितः।
कृष्णो विहरते रत्नमन्दिरं रासमण्डलम्॥१॥

evaṁ dinatrayaṁ tatra bhakteśvaravibhāvitaḥ|
kṛṣṇo viharate ratnamandiraṁ rāsamaṇḍalam||1||

evam — thus; dina-trayam — for three days; tatra — there; bhakta-ishvara-vibhavitah — as contemplated by the Lord of the devotees; krishnah — Krishna; viharate — sports; ratna-mandiram — in the jewelled temple; rasa-mandalam — in the circle of the rasa dance.

1Thus for three days Krishna sports there, in the jewelled temple, the circle of the rasa dance, as the Lord of the devotees beholds it.

Verse 2

नवदिनसमुदायं गुण्डिचाप्रेमवासं
गजपतिनृपसेव्ये नीलशैलाधिनाथे।
कृतवति जगदीशे साग्रजे गौरचन्द्रो
रथमनुगत एव भक्तवर्गेण सार्धम्॥२॥

navadinasamudāyaṁ guṇḍicāpremavāsaṁ
gajapatinṛpasevye nīlaśailādhināthe|
kṛtavati jagadīśe sāgraje gauracandro
rathamanugata eva bhaktavargeṇa sārdham||2||

nava-dina-samudayam — for the space of nine days; gundicha-prema-vasam — a loving stay at Gundicha; gajapati-nripa-sevye — served by the Gajapati king; nila-shaila-adhinathe — the Lord of the Blue Mountain; kritavati — when (He) had made; jagat-ishe — the Lord of the world; sa-agraje — with His elder brother; gaurachandrah — Gaurachandra; ratham — the chariot; anugatah — following; eva — indeed; bhakta-vargena sardham — together with the host of devotees.

2When the Lord of the world, the Master of the Blue Mountain, whom the Gajapati king serves, had stayed lovingly at Gundicha for nine days together with His elder brother, Gaurachandra, following His chariot with the whole host of devotees,

Verse 3

होरापञ्चमीयात्राश्च श्रीलक्ष्मीविजयोत्सवम्।
कृत्वा ययौ नीलशैलं श्रीलीलापुरुषोत्तमः॥३॥

horāpañcamīyātrāśca śrīlakṣmīvijayotsavam|
kṛtvā yayau nīlaśailaṁ śrīlīlāpuruṣottamaḥ||3||

hora-panchami-yatrah — the processions of Hora-panchami; cha — and; shri-lakshmi-vijaya-utsavam — the festival of Sri Lakshmi's victory; kritva — having celebrated; yayau — went; nila-shailam — to the Blue Mountain (Nilachala); shri-lila-purushottamah — Sri Purushottama of the pastimes.

3celebrated the processions of Hora-panchami and the festival of Sri Lakshmi's victory1; and then Sri Purushottama of the pastimes went to Nilachala.

Verse 4

ततः परं श्रीशचीनन्दनो हरिः
पद्मावतीनन्दनरामसङ्गतः।
श्रीरत्नसिंहासनमध्यसंस्थितं
रामानुजं पश्यति वैष्णवैः सह॥४॥

tataḥ paraṁ śrīśacīnandano hariḥ
padmāvatīnandanarāmasaṅgataḥ|
śrīratnasiṁhāsanamadhyasaṁsthitaṁ
rāmānujaṁ paśyati vaiṣṇavaiḥ saha||4||

tatah param — after that; shri-shachinandanah — Sri Shachinandana; harih — Hari; padmavati-nandana-rama-sangatah — together with Rama, the son of Padmavati; shri-ratna-simhasana-madhya-samsthitam — seated in the midst of the glorious jewelled throne; rama-anujam — the younger brother of Rama; pashyati — beholds; vaishnavaih saha — together with the Vaishnavas.

4After this Sri Shachinandana Hari, together with Rama, the son of Padmavati2, and with the Vaishnavas, beholds the younger brother of Rama seated in the midst of the glorious jewelled throne.

Verse 5

नीलाद्रौ शङ्खमध्ये शतदलकमले रत्नसिंहासनस्थं
सर्वालङ्कारयुक्तं नवघनरुचिरं संस्थितं चाग्रजेन।
भद्राया वामभागे रथचरणयुतं ब्रह्मरुद्रादिवन्द्यं
वेदानां सारमेकं सकलगुणमयं ब्रह्म पूर्णं स्मरामि॥५॥

nīlādrau śaṅkhamadhye śatadalakamale ratnasiṁhāsanasthaṁ
sarvālaṅkārayuktaṁ navaghanaruciraṁ saṁsthitaṁ cāgrajena|
bhadrāyā vāmabhāge rathacaraṇayutaṁ brahmarudrādivandyaṁ
vedānāṁ sāramekaṁ sakalaguṇamayaṁ brahma pūrṇaṁ smarāmi||5||

nila-adrau — on the Blue Mountain; shankha-madhye — in the midst of the Conch; shata-dala-kamale — on a hundred-petalled lotus; ratna-simhasana-stham — seated on a jewelled throne; sarva-alankara-yuktam — adorned with every ornament; nava-ghana-ruchiram — lovely as a fresh rain cloud; samsthitam — abiding; cha — and; agrajena — with His elder brother; bhadrayah — of Bhadra (Subhadra); vama-bhage — on the left side; ratha-charana-yutam — together with the wheel (Sudarshana); brahma-rudra-adi-vandyam — worshipped by Brahma, Rudra and the rest; vedanam — of the Vedas; saram — the essence; ekam — sole; sakala-guna-mayam — full of all qualities; brahma — the Brahman; purnam — complete; smarami — I remember.

5"On the Blue Mountain, in the midst of the Conch, on a hundred-petalled lotus, He sits upon a jewelled throne, adorned with every ornament, lovely as a fresh rain cloud, together with His elder brother; He is at Bhadra's left, and the wheel is with Him; Brahma, Rudra and the others worship Him. Him, the one essence of the Vedas, full of all qualities, the Supreme Brahman in His fullness3, I remember."

Verse 6

एवं ध्यात्वा गतः कृष्णो मिश्रस्य पुष्पवाटिकाम्।
सुखमासनमासित्वा भक्तान् गौडनिवासिनः॥६॥

evaṁ dhyātvā gataḥ kṛṣṇo miśrasya puṣpavāṭikām|
sukhamāsanamāsitvā bhaktān gauḍanivāsinaḥ||6||

evam — thus; dhyatva — having meditated; gatah — gone; krishnah — Krishna; mishrasya — of Mishra; pushpa-vatikam — to the flower garden; sukham — comfortably; asanam — on a seat; asitva — having sat; bhaktan — the devotees; gauda-nivasinah — dwelling in Gauda.

6Having meditated on Him thus, Krishna went to the flower garden of Mishra4, and, seated comfortably there, He sent home the devotees who lived in Gauda —

Verse 7

यापयामास भगवान् जनन्याः सुखहेतवे।
यातासौ श्रीहरेर्भक्तिरूपिणी प्रेमरूपिणी॥७॥

yāpayāmāsa bhagavān jananyāḥ sukhahetave|
yātāsau śrīharerbhaktirūpiṇī premarūpiṇī||7||

yapayamasa — sent back (home); bhagavan — the Lord; jananyah — of His mother; sukha-hetave — for the happiness; yata asau — for she (reading unclear); shri-hareh — of Sri Hari; bhakti-rupini — devotion embodied; prema-rupini — love embodied.

7the Lord sent them back for the happiness of His mother, for she is devotion to Sri Hari embodied, love embodied5.

Verse 8

नित्यानन्दं समालिङ्ग्य धृत्वा तस्य करद्वयम्।
प्राह सगद्गदं याहि गौडदेशं त्वमीश्वरः॥८॥

nityānandaṁ samāliṅgya dhṛtvā tasya karadvayam|
prāha sagadgadaṁ yāhi gauḍadeśaṁ tvamīśvaraḥ||8||

nityanandam — Nityananda; samalingya — embracing; dhritva — taking; tasya — His; kara-dvayam — two hands; praha — said; sa-gadgadam — in a faltering voice; yahi — go; gauda-desham — to the land of Gauda; tvam — You; ishvarah — the Lord.

8Embracing Nityananda and taking both His hands, He said in a faltering voice, "Go to Gauda: You are the Lord.

Verse 9

तव देहं विजानीयाद्विश्वासभरणं मम।
एतज्ज्ञात्वा यथेच्छं त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि हि प्रभो॥९॥

tava dehaṁ vijānīyādviśvāsabharaṇaṁ mama|
etajjñātvā yathecchaṁ tvaṁ kartumarhasi hi prabho||9||

tava — Your; deham — body; vijaniyat — let one know (as); vishvasa-bharanam — the bearer of the trust; mama — My; etat — this; jnatva — knowing; yatha-ichchham — as You wish; tvam — You; kartum — to act; arhasi — are free; hi — indeed; prabho — O Prabhu.

9Let it be known that Your body is the keeper of My trust. Knowing this, Prabhu, You are free to act as You wish.

Verse 10

मूर्खनीचजडान्धाख्या ये च पातकिनोऽपरे।
तानेव सर्वथा सर्वान् कुरु प्रेमाधिकारिणः॥१०॥

mūrkhanīcajaḍāndhākhyā ye ca pātakino'pare|
tāneva sarvathā sarvān kuru premādhikāriṇaḥ||10||

murkha-nicha-jada-andha-akhyah — those called fools, low, dull, blind; ye — who; cha — and; patakinah — sinners; apare — other; tan — them; eva — indeed; sarvatha — in every way; sarvan — all; kuru — make; prema-adhikarinah — worthy of love (for Krishna).

10Those who are called fools, low, dull and blind, and all other sinners — make every one of them worthy of love for Krishna."

Verse 11

तमिति प्रहसन् प्राह नर्तकोऽहं तव प्रभो।
करिष्यामि यथाज्ञा ते यतस्त्वं सूत्रधारकः॥११॥

tamiti prahasan prāha nartako'haṁ tava prabho|
kariṣyāmi yathājñā te yatastvaṁ sūtradhārakaḥ||11||

tam — to Him; iti — thus; prahasan — laughing; praha — said; nartakah — the dancer (actor); aham — I; tava — Your; prabho — O Prabhu; karishyami — I shall do; yatha — as; ajna — the command; te — Your; yatah — for; tvam — You; sutra-dharakah — the sutradhara (director of the play).

11Laughing, Nityananda replied, "Prabhu, I am Your dancer. I shall do as You command, for You are the director of the play6."

Verse 12

तयोरेवं कथयतोः स्वरूपादिगणैः सह।
पुरीश्रीपरमानन्दरामानन्दादिभिस्तथा॥१२॥

tayorevaṁ kathayatoḥ svarūpādigaṇaiḥ saha|
purīśrīparamānandarāmānandādibhistathā||12||

tayoh — while the two; evam — thus; kathayatoh — were conversing; svarupa-adi-ganaih saha — together with Svarupa and his company; puri-shri-paramananda-ramananda-adibhih — with Sri Paramananda Puri, Ramananda and others; tatha — likewise.

12While the two were talking thus in the company of Svarupa and his companions, of Sri Paramananda Puri, Ramananda and others,

Verse 13

द्राविडस्थो द्विजः कश्चिद्दरिद्रो बुद्धिसत्तमः।
आजगाम धनार्थं च जगन्नाथदिदृक्षया॥१३॥

drāviḍastho dvijaḥ kaściddaridro buddhisattamaḥ|
ājagāma dhanārthaṁ ca jagannāthadidṛkṣayā||13||

dravida-sthah — living in Dravida; dvijah — brahmana; kashchit — a certain; daridrah — poor; buddhi-sattamah — excellent in understanding; ajagama — came; dhana-artham — for the sake of wealth; cha — and; jagannatha-didrikshaya — with the desire to see Jagannatha.

13a certain poor brahmana from Dravida, a man of excellent understanding, arrived; he had come for wealth, and out of longing to see Jagannatha.

Verse 14

निवेद्य स्वप्रयोजनं जगन्नाथस्य सन्निधौ।
स्थितः सप्तदिनान्येव प्रत्यादेशं विचिन्तयन्॥१४॥

nivedya svaprayojanaṁ jagannāthasya sannidhau|
sthitaḥ saptadinānyeva pratyādeśaṁ vicintayan||14||

nivedya — having laid out; sva-prayojanam — his need; jagannathasya sannidhau — before Jagannatha; sthitah — remained; sapta-dinani — seven days; eva — indeed; pratyadesham — an answer (command); vichintayan — awaiting (pondering).

14Having laid his need before Jagannatha, he stayed there for seven whole days, awaiting an answer.

Verse 15

अप्राप्य वाञ्छितं दुःखात् समुद्रतीरमागतः।
तत्रैव ह्यागतं दैवाद्विभीषणं च दर्शयन्॥१५॥

aprāpya vāñchitaṁ duḥkhāt samudratīramāgataḥ|
tatraiva hyāgataṁ daivādvibhīṣaṇaṁ ca darśayan||15||

aprapya — not obtaining; vanchhitam — what he desired; duhkhat — out of sorrow; samudra-tiram — to the shore of the ocean; agatah — came; tatra eva — right there; hi — and lo; agatam — who had come; daivat — by providence; vibhishanam — Vibhishana; cha — and; darshayan — seeing (meeting).

15Not obtaining what he desired, he went in sorrow to the seashore, and there he met Vibhishana7, who by providence had come to the same place.

Verse 16

पप्रच्छ को भवान् कुत्र यासि स त्वं वदस्व भो।
सप्ताहं श्रीजगन्नाथदर्शनार्थं गतोऽप्यहम्॥१६॥

papraccha ko bhavān kutra yāsi sa tvaṁ vadasva bho|
saptāhaṁ śrījagannāthadarśanārthaṁ gato'pyaham||16||

papracchha — asked; kah — who; bhavan — are you (sir); kutra — where; yasi — are you going; sah tvam — you; vadasva — tell; bhoh — O; sapta-aham — for seven days; shri-jagannatha-darshana-artham — for the darshana of Sri Jagannatha; gatah — have gone; api — indeed; aham — I.

16He asked him, "Tell me, who are you, and where are you going? I have been going for seven days to have the darshana of Sri Jagannatha."

Verse 17

विभीषणो नाम मह्यमित्युक्त्वा प्रययौ स च।
विप्रोऽपि तेन सार्धं च ययौ सौभाग्यपर्वतः॥१७॥

vibhīṣaṇo nāma mahyamityuktvā prayayau sa ca|
vipro'pi tena sārdhaṁ ca yayau saubhāgyaparvataḥ||17||

vibhishanah — Vibhishana; nama — by name; mahyam — mine (is the name); iti — thus; uktva — saying; prayayau — went on; sah — he; cha — and; viprah — the brahmana; api — too; tena sardham — with him; cha — and; yayau — went; saubhagya-parvatah — a mountain of good fortune (supremely fortunate).

17"My name is Vibhishana," he answered, and went on his way; and the brahmana — truly a mountain of good fortune — went along with him.

Verse 18

आगतो गौरचन्द्रस्य समीपं श्रीविभीषणः।
दृष्ट्वा श्रीचरणद्वन्द्वं तस्य दण्डनतिर्भुवि॥१८॥

āgato gauracandrasya samīpaṁ śrīvibhīṣaṇaḥ|
dṛṣṭvā śrīcaraṇadvandvaṁ tasya daṇḍanatirbhuvi||18||

agatah — came; gaurachandrasya — of Gaurachandra; samipam — to the presence; shri-vibhishanah — Sri Vibhishana; drishtva — seeing; shri-charana-dvandvam — the pair of holy feet; tasya — his; danda-natih — obeisance (falling) like a rod; bhuvi — on the ground.

18Sri Vibhishana came to Gaurachandra, and seeing His holy feet he fell to the ground like a rod.

Verse 19

विप्रोऽपि स चमत्कारं पश्यन् प्रेमपरिप्लुतः।
दारिद्र्यं श्लाघयन् दुःखं ननर्त जातकौतुकः॥१९॥

vipro'pi sa camatkāraṁ paśyan premapariplutaḥ|
dāridryaṁ ślāghayan duḥkhaṁ nanarta jātakautukaḥ||19||

viprah — brahmana; api — and; sah — that; chamatkaram — the wonder; pashyan — seeing; prema-pariplutah — flooded with love; daridryam — his poverty; shlaghayan — praising; duhkham — his sorrow; nanarta — danced; jata-kautukah — overcome with delight.

19Seeing this wonder, the brahmana, flooded with love, began to praise his poverty and his sorrow, and danced in delight.

Verse 20

विभीषणं च भगवान् वाञ्छाकल्पतरुः प्रभुः।
प्राह ब्राह्मणवर्याय धनं दत्त्वा भवान् खलु॥२०॥

vibhīṣaṇaṁ ca bhagavān vāñchākalpataruḥ prabhuḥ|
prāha brāhmaṇavaryāya dhanaṁ dattvā bhavān khalu||20||

vibhishanam — to Vibhishana; cha — and; bhagavan — the Lord; vanchha-kalpa-taruh — the wish-fulfilling tree; prabhuh — the Master; praha — said; brahmana-varyaya — to the best of brahmanas; dhanam — wealth; dattva — giving; bhavan — you; khalu — indeed.

20Then the Lord, the Master, the wish-fulfilling tree, said to Vibhishana, "Give wealth to this best of brahmanas,

Verse 21

पूर्णयिष्यति येनासौ दुःखरोगाद्विमुच्यते।
कृताञ्जलिपुटः सोऽपि जग्राह शिरसि वचः॥२१॥

pūrṇayiṣyati yenāsau duḥkharogādvimucyate|
kṛtāñjalipuṭaḥ so'pi jagrāha śirasi vacaḥ||21||

purnayishyati — will satisfy (him); yena — whereby; asau — he; duhkha-rogat — from the disease of sorrow; vimuchyate — is freed; krita-anjali-putah — with joined palms; sah — he (Vibhishana); api — too; jagraha — took; shirasi — on his head; vachah — the words.

21and satisfy him, so that he may be freed from the disease of sorrow." With joined palms Vibhishana took these words upon his head.

Verse 22

श्रुत्वा द्विजवरः प्राह मा मां संत्यक्तुमर्हसि।
यथा ते चरणप्राप्तिस्तथा कुरु जगद्गुरो॥२२॥

śrutvā dvijavaraḥ prāha mā māṁ saṁtyaktumarhasi|
yathā te caraṇaprāptistathā kuru jagadguro||22||

shrutva — hearing; dvija-varah — the best of brahmanas; praha — said; ma — do not; mam — me; samtyaktum arhasi — please abandon; yatha — so that; te — Your; charana-praptih — attainment of the feet; tatha — so; kuru — do; jagat-guro — O Teacher of the world.

22Hearing this, the best of brahmanas said, "Do not abandon me! Grant that I may attain Your feet, O Teacher of the world!

Verse 23

जगन्नाथ हृषीकेश संसारार्णवतारक।
पतितप्रेमदः कृष्णस्त्वमेव मां समुद्धर॥२३॥

jagannātha hṛṣīkeśa saṁsārārṇavatāraka|
patitapremadaḥ kṛṣṇastvameva māṁ samuddhara||23||

jagannatha — O Lord of the world; hrishikesha — O Hrishikesha; samsara-arnava-taraka — O You who carry across the ocean of samsara; patita-prema-dah — the giver of love to the fallen; krishnah — Krishna; tvam eva — You Yourself; mam — me; samuddhara — deliver.

23O Jagannatha, Hrishikesha, You who carry souls across the ocean of samsara! You Yourself are Krishna, who gives love to the fallen: deliver me!"

Verse 24

तं प्राह करुणासिन्धुर्याहि त्वं निजमन्दिरम्।
भुक्त्वा भोगान् समुत्सृज्य श्रीकृष्णचरणं सदा॥२४॥

taṁ prāha karuṇāsindhuryāhi tvaṁ nijamandiram|
bhuktvā bhogān samutsṛjya śrīkṛṣṇacaraṇaṁ sadā||24||

tam — to him; praha — said; karuna-sindhuh — the ocean of compassion; yahi — go; tvam — you; nija-mandiram — to your own home; bhuktva — having enjoyed; bhogan — the pleasures; samutsrijya — having given (them) up; shri-krishna-charanam — the feet of Sri Krishna; sada — always.

24The ocean of compassion said to him, "Go to your home. Enjoy these goods, and then give them up8: one who constantly worships the feet of Sri Krishna

Verse 25

भजनाल्लभते भक्तिं यथा स्यात् प्रेमसम्पदः।
एवं श्रुत्वा प्रणम्यासौ ययौ निजगृहं द्विजः॥२५॥

bhajanāllabhate bhaktiṁ yathā syāt premasampadaḥ|
evaṁ śrutvā praṇamyāsau yayau nijagṛhaṁ dvijaḥ||25||

bhajanat — by worship (of the feet); labhate — one attains; bhaktim — devotion; yatha — so that; syat — there will be; prema-sampadah — the wealth of love; evam — thus; shrutva — having heard; pranamya — bowing; asau — he; yayau — went; nija-griham — home; dvijah — the brahmana.

25attains devotion, and the wealth of love comes to him." Hearing this, the brahmana bowed down and went home.

Verse 26

विभीषणश्च तं स्तुत्वा प्रणम्य च पुनः पुनः।
जगाम स्वगृहं रम्यं ध्यायन् तच्चरणाम्बुजम्॥२६॥

vibhīṣaṇaśca taṁ stutvā praṇamya ca punaḥ punaḥ|
jagāma svagṛhaṁ ramyaṁ dhyāyan taccaraṇāmbujam||26||

vibhishanah — Vibhishana; cha — and; tam — Him; stutva — having praised; pranamya — bowing; cha — and; punah punah — again and again; jagama — went; sva-griham — to his own home; ramyam — lovely; dhyayan — meditating on; tat-charana-ambujam — His lotus feet.

26And Vibhishana, having praised Him and bowed again and again, went to his lovely home, meditating on His lotus feet.

Thus ends the twenty-first sarga, "Grace to Ramadasa"9, of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Hora-panchami (usually Hera-panchami): the fifth day after the chariots set out, when Lakshmi, left behind in the temple, comes to Gundicha in search of Jagannatha; the "festival of Lakshmi's victory" is the celebration connected with her coming.
  2. Padmavati is the mother of Nityananda; Rama is Nityananda (Balarama). "The younger brother of Rama" is Krishna, that is, Jagannatha.
  3. A meditation from the Puranas: Puri (Sri Kshetra) has the shape of a conch; "the wheel" is the Sudarshana. "The Supreme Brahman" here is not an impersonal effulgence but the Lord Jagannatha Himself, possessed of form, ornaments and all qualities (cf. Bhagavad-gita 14.27: "I am the basis of Brahman").
  4. Probably Kashi Mishra, in whose house the Lord lived at Puri.
  5. The reading of this passage in the editions is corrupt; the translation follows the sense.
  6. The sutradhara: the director of a stage play, "the holder of the strings"; all His companions are actors in His lila.
  7. Vibhishana: Ravana's brother, the great devotee of Ramachandra, who received long life from Him; tradition holds that he comes to Puri for the darshana of Jagannatha.
  8. The Lord, fulfilling His command to Vibhishana, lets the poor brahmana accept the wealth given him, but shows the goal: not to cling to it but to serve Krishna's feet — then devotion and the wealth of love will come (v. 25).
  9. Ramadasa means "servant of Rama." The name does not occur in the text of the sarga; probably Vibhishana, the servant of Ramachandra, is meant (the Lord also gave this name to Murari himself; see 2.07.18).
